verdict.rationale: Bolt provides mechanisms that could support safe iteration—direct code view editing, GitHub backup/version history for reverting changes—but hands-on community reports concretely contradict the 'without breaking what works' promise: one user described a 'doom loop where there is a cycle of breakage, each fix resurrecting a previous break,' another reported the AI making unauthorized destructive changes and burning tokens on unneeded fixes, and a third's tip was to avoid trying to fix mistakes and instead revert and re-prompt because context gets polluted. Missing for 10: first-party evidence of safeguards against regression, and any hands-on account showing iterative prompting reliably preserves prior functionality.
